newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba declines comment on market variable repo talk.
newsitem.headline: Buba declines comment on market variable repo talk.

text.p: The Bundesbank on Thursday declined to comment on market speculation that its council had on Thursday empowered its Frankfurt directorate to switch to a variable rate securities repurchase tender in two weeks' time.
"We do not comment on market rumours," a central bank spokesman said, giving the central bank's standard response to market speculation.

The Bundesbank earlier surprised markets by setting securities repurchase tenders at a fixed rate of three percent for the next two weeks only, leaving open the question of exactly where the repo rate will be in the second half of its four-week summer break.
In the past, the Bundesbank has generally set fixed rate tenders throughout holiday periods when this has been the form in which it has been providing funds to the money market.
Under a fixed rate repo, the Bundesbank only offers funds at a single specified rate. In a variable rate pact, banks bid at the interest rates of their choice.

A full meeting of the central bank council is not needed to change the repo rate. But in an instance where a change in the rate -- or in the type of tender adopted -- was needed, the council as a whole would usually give guidance to those making the decision.
This need not take the form of a specific instruction, but could offer a range of possibilities to those who will make a final decision.

The next securities repurchase tender for which no conditions have yet been set would normally be extended to the market on August 12. It was not immediately clear when details of that pact would be released.
